observations.attempt: This is the diff's central security-relevant change (GAP-4). Cold-modeled the attack: (1) capture a genuine (rawBody, X-Hub-Signature-256) pair; (2) resubmit it with a freshly-generated X-GitHub-Delivery header, hoping the receiver treats it as a new, undeduped event. Read githubDeliveryIdentity.ts: githubWebhookIdempotencyKey(rawBody) is a pure, single-argument function of the raw body bytes only — it has no access to any header, and its arity (verified structurally by a dedicated test asserting `.length === 1`) makes it impossible to smuggle X-GitHub-Delivery into the digest without changing the function's signature. Confirmed githubWebhookService.ts step (h) passes `input.rawBody` (not deliveryId) into this function, and deliveryId is used only for `trace_id`/`payload.delivery_id`. Verified: (a) SHA-256 preimage/second-preimage resistance makes forcing a chosen collision computationally infeasible; (b) the signature gate (ING-01) runs strictly before idempotency-key derivation, so an attacker without the shared secret cannot even reach this code path with an attacker-chosen body; (c) tested EC-2's exact scenario via githubWebhookService.gapfill.test.ts and the fixtures replay test — same bytes + different delivery headers -> identical idempotency_key and identical BullMQ jobId; (d) tested EC-3 — single-byte-different bodies -> different keys (no accidental collapse of two distinct real events); (e) checked downstream consumers: SQS's messageDeduplicationId() re-hashes the already-79-char key with its own SHA-256 (queue/bullmq.ts:155-160) — no truncation-induced collision risk since the transport ID is itself a fixed-width digest of the full semantic key; BullMQ's jobId is the raw idempotency_key string passed through enqueue() with no truncation (queue/bullmq.ts:227+). No forcible collision, no predictability, no pre-signature-verification exposure found.

observations.attempt: Modeled an attacker (or GitHub itself, on a slow retry) replaying a captured, validly-signed (body, signature) pair AFTER the SQS FIFO 5-minute dedup window has expired, or after the original BullMQ job has completed and its record was erased by `removeOnComplete: true`. Confirmed GAP-4's fix makes the dedup IDENTITY itself untamperable (ING-02, PASS) but does not extend the WINDOW during which that identity is enforced: SQS FIFO natively bounds MessageDeduplicationId enforcement to 5 minutes, and queue/bullmq.ts:256 still sets `removeOnComplete: true`, which erases BullMQ's own jobId record once the job completes — a replay after either point is not rejected by Core and would re-publish/re-enqueue as if it were new work. This is a genuine, currently-exploitable duplicate-processing window, not merely theoretical. It is explicitly disclosed and deliberately out of this gapfill's scope: spec.md's Open Questions #1 names it directly ("SQS FIFO dedup is 5 minutes... BullMQ's jobId record is erased by enqueue's removeOnComplete: true... A persisted delivery log plus removeOnComplete:{age} is the audit's recommended fix... but was NOT filed as a gap; it needs a migration and a queue-wide behavior change"), citing docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-04-webhooks-git.md's own MEDIUM rating for the same finding. Not a regression: this window existed identically before this diff (the old delivery-id-derived key had the same window, plus was additionally forgeable — GAP-4 strictly improves the identity while leaving the window unchanged). No formal risk-acceptance record (named approver, reason, ticket, expiry per audit-contract.md section 7) exists anywhere in .pipeline/ — only narrative disclosure in spec.md's Open Questions — so this cannot be marked RISK_ACCEPTED; recorded OPEN.
